note: GDPR submodule for Subject Access Request (SAR) and Right-to-be-Forgotten task workflow. Content entity gdpr_task with config bundle entity gdpr_task_type (config_prefix gdpr_task_type; default types gdpr_sar 'SARs Request' and gdpr_remove 'Removal request'). Routes: create /user/{user}/gdpr-request/{gdpr_task_type} (gdpr_tasks.request), list /admin/config/gdpr/tasks, summary /admin/config/gdpr/summary, removal settings /admin/config/gdpr/remove-settings. Services gdpr_tasks.manager, gdpr_tasks.anonymizer, rta/rtf traversal factories; queue worker gdpr_tasks_process_gdpr_sar; field type gdpr_task_item; Rules events gdpr_tasks.rules_rta_complete / _rtf_complete. Permissions create/view gdpr tasks, add/administer/delete/edit/view task entities, view gdpr data summary. Requires gdpr, anonymizer, gdpr_fields, entity, file, views, options. Medium/hard are grounded in the RemovalSettingsForm config gdpr_tasks.settings (key export_directory) - a SIMPLE config object that does NOT trigger a route rebuild (creating/deleting a gdpr_task_type bundle would, and this shared site has a pre-existing workbench_moderation route-rebuild fatal at terminate). NOTE: this campaign completed the submodule's entity-schema install that was skipped during the site's enable window.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal gdpr_tasks module manage, what content entity and bundle does it use, and what are its two default task types?
evals.expected_output: It manages GDPR data requests via the gdpr_task content entity with the gdpr_task_type config bundle. Two default types ship: gdpr_sar (SARs Request - Subject Access Request/export) and gdpr_remove (Removal request - Right to be Forgotten).

evals.prompt: In gdpr_tasks, what is the route/path to create a GDPR data request for a user, and where is the Right-to-be-Forgotten export directory configured?
evals.expected_output: Create a request at /user/{user}/gdpr-request/{gdpr_task_type} (route gdpr_tasks.request, permission 'create gdpr tasks'). The removal export directory is set on the Right to be Forgotten settings form at /admin/config/gdpr/remove-settings (stored in config gdpr_tasks.settings, key export_directory).

evals.prompt: How does gdpr_tasks build a subject's data for a SAR export or removal, and which service/queue worker is involved?
evals.expected_output: It uses GDPR Fields' metadata and entity-traversal services (gdpr_tasks.rta_traversal / gdpr_tasks.rtf_traversal, built via EntityTraversalFactory) to walk the subject's data graph following configured relationships. A SAR export is assembled by the queue worker gdpr_tasks_process_gdpr_sar (zip), and removal anonymizes fields via gdpr_tasks.anonymizer using each field's RTF setting.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, gdpr_tasks has its Right-to-be-Forgotten export directory configured. Inspect the live configuration and state the export directory path.
evals.expected_output: In config gdpr_tasks.settings, export_directory = 'private://gdpr-eval-export' (the directory where processed removal tasks are exported).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure gdpr_tasks so that processed Right-to-be-Forgotten (removal) tasks are exported to the directory 'private://gdpr-export'. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Config gdpr_tasks.settings has a non-empty export_directory (e.g. 'private://gdpr-export'). Set it via the Right to be Forgotten settings form (/admin/config/gdpr/remove-settings) or by saving the gdpr_tasks.settings config's export_directory key.
